projection: 2:1 dimetric, orthographic, camera elevation 30 deg: one ground metre is pxPerMetre wide along screen x and half of that along screen y
aimZero: frame 0 aims along grid +x (screen lower-right); frames advance with atan2(dy, dx) in grid cells, i.e. clockwise on screen
sheets: towers/<model>_L<level>@1x.json or @2x.json (PixiJS spritesheet); draw <base> first, then <aim>_NN on top, both at the tower's ground point

fire.frameForAim: DD = Math.round(aim / (2 * Math.PI / dirs)) mod dirs, two digits
fire.use: on a shot draw the frames of direction DD instead of the aim layer (base stays); frames 1..releaseFrame-1 at fps, the round leaves at releaseFrame (muzzle point), play on to reloadFrom-1, then spread reloadFrom..frames over the reload time; after the last frame show the aim layer again

field.note: seamless in both screen directions; draw as a tiling sprite at the same pxPerMetre as the towers

road.note: seamless in both screen directions; draw as a tiling sprite at the same pxPerMetre as the towers

drone.shadow: no shadow in the sprite: draw a dark ellipse on the ground below it

enemiesNote: enemies/<model>@1x|@2x.json: frame <model>_NN faces game angle NN * 2*pi/directions (atan2(dy, dx) in grid cells, 0 = screen lower-right); anchor = the unit's ground centre; shadow included. With a 'move' entry, <model>_NN_FF are its movement frames (animation <model>_NN_move); <model>_NN stays the still (= frame 00). Distance-driven (cycleM set): frame = floor((distance / cycleM + phase) * frames) mod frames, phase a random 0..1 per unit; time-driven (fps set): frame = floor(t * fps + phase * frames) mod frames.

muzzle_flash.note: flame points along +x: rotate the sprite to the barrel's screen angle

fire_stream.note: jet along +x from the nozzle: rotate to the nozzle's screen angle, scale x to the range; loop while firing

fire_burn.note: flames on a burning target or ground patch; loop

rail_charge.note: charging glow at the muzzle; loop while charging

rail_beam.note: shot line along +x from the muzzle: rotate to the target, scale x to the distance; play once

smoke_plume.note: dark smoke column over a damaged building or gun; loop. Pair with fire_burn at the breach; anchor = the base of the column

scorpion.note: one frame per flight heading (frame = round(angle / (2pi / frames)) mod frames), no shadow: draw a dark ellipse on the ground below it

trebuchet.note: tumbling round, no shadow: draw a dark ellipse on the ground below it

crossbow.note: one frame per flight heading (frame = round(angle / (2pi / frames)) mod frames), no shadow: draw a dark ellipse on the ground below it

zadnoper.note: one frame per flight heading (frame = round(angle / (2pi / frames)) mod frames), no shadow: draw a dark ellipse on the ground below it

fencesNote: fences/<material>@1x|@2x.json, frames <material>_<piece>, anchor = ground point of the tile centre. Per tile draw <material>_post, then the half-segments toward each fenced neighbour: px (+x), nx (-x), py (+y), ny (-y) in grid cells. Draw order: segments behind the post (ny, nx) first, then post, then py, px; sort tiles back to front as usual.
buildingsNote: buildings/<id>@1x|@2x.json, frame <id>_L<n> for level n (1-based; the game's level index 0 = L1). Anchor = ground point of the building's centre (the middle of its 2x2 tiles); the frame is taller than wide, so anchor.y is below the middle. One static frame per level; draw in the normal depth sort with the guns. Damage: states.sheet (buildings/<id>_states@1x|@2x) holds states.damaged[n-1] (below half health: a breach in the front-right corner), states.rubble[n-1] (destroyed) and, for hq only, states.occupied[n-1] (taken by the Iron Concord); same frame size and anchor as the level frames. Put effects fire_burn + smoke_plume on damaged ones.
wreckNote: towers.<id>.levels[].states.wreck = {sheet, frame}: the destroyed gun, one static frame per level, drawn alone instead of base + aim, same anchor as the base frame. Damaged guns (below half health) keep their normal frames with the looping effects fire_small and smoke_plume on top.
alliesNote: allies/<id>: the player's own units (raiders = the party that rides out to provoke the enemy). Same sheet layout, headings and movement as enemies.
